applies_to: Eaton IQ 250 and IQ 260 meters (including the L logging versions), Modbus map Appendix B of IB02601006E.
summary: The IQ 250 and IQ 260 are panel-mount multifunction power meters with a serial COM2 port (Modbus RTU, Modbus ASCII or DNP) and optional plug-in cards, including a network card for Modbus TCP. Everything sits in holding registers: live readings and demand values are IEEE floats in primary units, while status, THD and angles are 16-bit integers. This map covers identification, primary readings, demand, maximum demand, phase angles, status, THD, reset commands and the CT/PT and COM2 settings.

addressing.note: Each map row prints a hex address and a decimal register. The hex column is the wire address; the decimal column is one higher (the map's own example: serial number at hex 0008 = register 9, entered as 40009 in a SCADA tool). Here 'documented' is the decimal register and address = decimal minus 1.

source.title: Appendix B: IQ 250/260 Meter, IQ 250/260 Modbus Map
source.pages: Data formats pp. B-1 to B-3; register map MM-1 to MM-43 (PDF pages 25-67)

notes: Word order: the map's data-format preface says that for 32-bit integers and floats the lower-addressed register holds the high-order half, and its worked float example (C4E1 then 1DB9 = -1800.929) confirms it. All 32-bit values here are ABCD.

Eaton publishes this map on its Power Xpert Meter 2000 product page under a file name that also mentions the PXM 2000, but the document text itself only names the IQ 250/260. This entry is therefore limited to the IQ 250/260.

Left out: the integer Readings Block (registers 279-305). Its scale and decimal-point position come from the programmable settings, so a fixed scale cannot be given. Use the float Primary Readings Block instead.

Left out: every energy counter (Primary Energy Block 1500-1571, Uncompensated energy 3032-3103 and the secondary-block energy 40022-40061). They are signed or unsigned 32-bit integers whose implied decimal point and unit/kilo/mega multiplier depend on the Power & Energy Format register (30006), which the schema cannot express as a fixed scale. Read 30006 and apply its energy scale and decimal digits yourself if you need them.
Left out: the secondary readings block 40002-40073. These values use offset formulas such as 150 x (raw - 2047) / 2047 that do not fit a simple scale and offset.

Left out: short-term and minimum/maximum blocks other than the maximum demand values, timestamped min/max blocks, option-card blocks, log setup and log retrieval blocks, TSTAMP registers (three-register date/time) and the limit setpoints.
Map typo, not used here: in the Short Term Primary Maximum block, Volts C-N Maximum is printed with hex 232F-2320 against decimal 8992-8993; the decimal column implies hex 231F.
Values marked 'M' in the source range column mean a 1,000,000 multiplier on the range only; the floats themselves are in plain volts, amps, watts, VARs and VAs.
Command registers always read 0. If a password is wrong the meter still answers normally but does nothing; with passwords disabled the password is 5555.

integration.summary: Poll holding registers 999-1028 (wire) with function 03 to get voltages, currents, totals, PF and frequency as big-endian floats in primary units; read the demand block at 1999 and the status word at 4500. Settings changes need a password-protected privileged session and settings-update mode.
integration.enable: Reads need no enabling. To change settings: write the password to Open Privileged Command Session (21002), then Initiate Programmable Settings Update (21003), write the settings, use the checksum registers 21004/21005 (writing 21005 saves the settings to non-volatile memory), then write Terminate (21007), which restarts the meter. Reset commands (20000, 20001) take the password directly.
quirks: Holding registers only; the map has no input registers.
The printed decimal register is one higher than the wire address; the printed hex column is the wire address.
Per-phase power and power factor read zero unless the hookup is wye.
Registers not in the map read 0 and accept writes that do nothing.
setup: Set the COM2 address, baud rate and protocol from the front panel or Eaton's configuration software; over Modbus they live in 30026-30027 and can only be written in settings-update mode.
COM2 baud choices in the map: 9600, 19200, 38400 or 57600.
gotchas: Meter Data readings are 0 until the first measurements are ready and while the meter is in settings-update mode (measurement state 'off').
Reset energy after changing the Power & Energy Format register, as the map advises.
A THD register reading raw 10000 means THD is unavailable (low signal, delta voltage, or model).

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
note: Re-typed from the manufacturer's public documentation (see source) and verified against it. Registers vary by firmware and options; verify against the live device before writing.
